titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Fáriz and Galve besiege Alcocer; the sally, and Per Vermudoz charges with the banner (tiradas 32–34, lines 623–714)
part: Tiradas 32–34 · Fáriz and Galve besiege Alcocer; the sally, and Per Vermudoz charges with the banner (lines 623–714)

sentences.t:
Mio Çid con esta ganançia en Alcoçer está;
fizo enbiar por la tienda que dexara allá.
sentences.l:
My Çid with this gain in Alcoçer is;
he-made to-send for the tent that he-had-left there.
sentences.i: My Çid, with this gain, is in Alcocer; he sent back for the tent he had left behind.
sentences.n: Tirada 32 (assonance á) — the king of Valencia wants Alcocer back and sends an army against the Çid (Pidal: El rey de Valencia quiere recobrar a Alcocer. — Envía un ejército contra el Cid). A single stressed á closes every line (está, allá, va, Bivar, ha …); the lines in á-e are discussed below (v. 625). ganançia, 'gain, booty': the captured town and its wealth. fizo enbiar por, 'had someone sent for' (fazer + infinitive, 'to cause to be done'; f- for modern h-). dexara, the old -ra form with its original pluperfect sense, 'had left': the one tent left standing as a decoy in the feigned retreat (v. 576).

sentences.t:
Mucho pesa a los de Teca e a los de Ter[rer] non plaze,
e a los de Calatayuth [sabet, pesando va.]
sentences.l:
Much it-weighs on those of Teca and to those of Ter[rer] not it-pleases,
and to those of Calatayuth [know-ye, grieving it-goes.]
sentences.i: The men of Ateca are sorely grieved, the men of Terrer are not pleased, and to the men of Calatayud, mark you, it was a heavy grief.
sentences.n: Teca = Ateca, Ter[rer] = Terrer, Calatayuth = Calatayud, the neighbouring towns of v. 570–572 (the last syllable of Terrer is Pidal's, as before). pesar a uno, 'to grieve someone'; non plaze, 'it does not please' — litotes. plaze ends in á-e, not plain á: Old Spanish verse admits a paragogic (added) -e after stressed á, so plaze, partes (648), grandes (653), Galve (654) and mensaje (627) all count as á-endings; the minstrel could equally sing them as plaz, part, grand. The whole second half of v. 626, [sabet, pesando va], is in italics in Pidal's print, i.e. supplied by him (it echoes sabet … pesava of v. 572); the manuscript's own ending is not given here, so the half-line is his conjecture. sabet, 'know ye', the minstrel's aside; pesando va, ir + gerund, 'it goes grieving' = 'it grieves'.

sentences.t:
Al rey de Valençia enbiaron con mensaje,
que a uno que dizien mio Çid R[o]y Díaz de Bivar
“ayrólo rey Alfonsso, de tierra echado lo ha,
sentences.l:
To-the king of Valencia they-sent with message,
that to one whom they-called my Çid R[o]y Díaz of Bivar
“angered-at-him king Alfonsso, from land cast-out him he-has,
sentences.i: They sent word to the king of Valencia that one whom they called my Çid Ruy Díaz of Vivar — “King Alfonso turned his anger on him and has cast him out of the land;
sentences.n: The message is half reported (que a uno …, 'that one …') and then slips into the townsmen's own voice; Pidal opens the quotation at v. 629 and it runs to v. 635. The que a uno clause is never completed as grammar: the speaker starts over with the direct words. dizien, 'they called' (imperfect, 3rd plural, impersonal). R[o]y = Ruy (only the o is Pidal's). ayrólo, 'was angered at him' (airar + lo): the ira regia, the king's formal disfavour that sent the Çid into exile. echado lo ha, 'he has cast him out' (participle + pronoun + auxiliary). mensaje: another á-e line in the á tirada.

sentences.t:
vino posar sobre Alcoçer, en un tan fuerte logar;
sacólos a çelada, el castiello ganado a;
sentences.l:
he-came to-camp over Alcoçer, in a so strong place;
he-drew-them into ambush, the castle won he-has;
sentences.i: he came and camped above Alcocer, in so strong a place; he drew them out into an ambush, and he has won the castle.
sentences.n: vino posar, 'came to camp': verbs of motion take a bare infinitive. sobre, 'over, above, against' (he camped on the hill over it, v. 557). sacólos a çelada, 'drew them out into an ambush' — the townsmen recount the stratagem of tirada 29 (cf. v. 579 por sacarlos a çelada). ganado a = ha ganado, 'has won'; the h of the auxiliary is not written.

sentences.t:
si non das consejo, a Teca e a Ter[rer] perderás,
perderás Calatayuth, que non puede escapar,
sentences.l:
if not you-give counsel, Teca and Ter[rer] you-will-lose,
you-will-lose Calatayuth, which not can escape,
sentences.i: If you give no help, you will lose Ateca and Terrer; you will lose Calatayud, which cannot hold out;
sentences.n: si non das consejo: Pidal glosses 'si no nos das ayuda', 'if you do not give us help' — consejo here is 'remedy, aid', not advice. perderás … perderás: the repetition across the line-break is a deliberate rhetorical push. que non puede escapar, 'which cannot escape' (fall to the Çid).

sentences.t:
ribera de Salón toda irá a mal,
assí ferá lo de Siloca, que es del otra part.”
sentences.l:
bank of Salón all will-go to ill,
so will-do that of Siloca, which is of-the other side.”
sentences.i: the whole valley of the Jalón will go to ruin, and so will the Jiloca's, which lies on the other side.”
sentences.n: ribera de Salón, 'the riverside of the Jalón' (Salón, the river Jalón, as v. 577). irá a mal, 'will go to ill, be lost'. ferá = hará, 'will do' (fazer, f- for h-). lo de Siloca, 'that of the Jiloca', the lands along the Jiloca, which joins the Jalón at Calatayud. del otra part: del before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (cf. el arrancada, v. 609); part = parte, cut. End of the townsmen's message.

sentences.t:
Quando lo o[d]ió rey Tamín por cuer le pesó mal:
“Tres reyes veo de moros, derredor de mí estar,
sentences.l:
When it heard king Tamín through heart to-him it-weighed ill:
“Three kings I-see of Moors, around of me to-be,
sentences.i: When King Tamín heard it, it grieved him to the heart: “I see three Moorish kings here about me;
sentences.n: o[d]ió = oyó, 'heard' (the d is Pidal's; odir is the old form of oír). Tamín: Pidal says flatly that no king Tamín of Valencia ever existed — 'No existió nunca un rey Tamín de Valencia' — Valencia was then ruled by Abu Béquer ben Abdelázíz, and in any case the lands of Calatayud belonged to the king of Zaragoza, not Valencia: 'El poeta fantasea aquí a su capricho' ('the poet invents freely here'). Fáriz and Galve too, he says, are fictional. por cuer, 'to the heart' (cuer = corazón). reyes de moros, Pidal: simply emirs or Muslim commanders, not kings of any territory. Tamín's speech runs to v. 642.

sentences.t:
non lo detardedes, los dos id por allá,
tres mill moros levedes con armas de lidiar;
sentences.l:
not it you-delay, the two go over there,
three thousand Moors you-take with arms of fighting;
sentences.i: do not delay — two of you go there, and take three thousand Moors with weapons for battle;
sentences.n: non lo detardedes, 'do not delay it' (negative command in the subjunctive; detardar as v. 575). los dos id, 'you two, go': id, imperative of ir. levedes, 'take' (subjunctive as command, from levar 'to carry, take'). armas de lidiar, 'arms for fighting' (lidiar, 'to fight a battle').

sentences.i: with the frontier men, who will help you, take him alive for me and bring him before me; since he has thrust himself into my land, he will have to give me satisfaction.”
sentences.n: los de la frontera, the garrisons of the border towns (Pidal on v. 698: the troops of the frontier towns, cf. vv. 640, 653). prendétmelo = prended + me + lo, 'take him for me' (imperative in -t for -d, the me an ethical dative); a vida, 'alive'. aduzidmelo, 'bring him to me' (aduzir, Latin adducere); delant = delante, cut. se me entró, 'entered on me' — the me marks Tamín as the injured party. derecho me avrá a dar, 'he will have to give me right', i.e. legal satisfaction, amends. delant ends in plain á; in this tirada á and á-e both pass.

sentences.t:
Tres mil moros cavalgan e pienssan de andar,
ellos vinieron a la noch en Sogorve posar.
sentences.l:
Three thousand Moors ride and they-think to go,
they came at the night in Sogorve to-camp.
sentences.i: Three thousand Moors mount and set out; that night they came to Segorbe and camped.
sentences.n: mil here, mill in v. 639: Pidal's text keeps the variation. pienssan de andar, 'set about going' (pensar de + infinitive, the stock formula). a la noch, 'at nightfall'; noch = noche, cut. Sogorve = Segorbe (province of Castellón). Pidal: the route the minstrel traces — Segorbe, Cella, Calatayud — shows that the Roman road from Sagunto to Bilbilis (Calatayud) was still in use.

sentences.t:
Otro día mañana pienssan de cavalgar,
vinieron a la noch a Çelfa posar.
sentences.l:
Other day morning they-think to ride,
they-came at the night at Çelfa to-camp.
sentences.i: Next morning they set off riding, and that night they came to Cella and camped.
sentences.n: Otro día mañana, 'the next morning', the poem's regular formula. Çelfa: Pidal identifies it as the older Celha, today Cella, three leagues from Teruel, 'con importantes ruinas romanas'. The two couplets (vv. 643–646) are built to the same pattern: departure, night, camp.

sentences.t:
Por los de la frontera pienssan de enviar;
non lo detienen, vienen de todas partes.
sentences.l:
For those of the frontier they-think to send;
not it they-delay, they-come from all parts.
sentences.i: They send for the frontier men; these lose no time, and come in from every side.
sentences.n: pienssan de enviar, 'they set about sending'. non lo detienen, 'they do not hold it back', i.e. they come at once (detener, 'to delay'). partes: á-e again in the á tirada (see v. 625).

sentences.t:
Ixieron de Çelfa la que dizen de Canal,
andidieron todo 'l día, que vagar non se dan,
vinieron essa noche en Calatayu[t]h posar.
sentences.l:
They-went-out from Çelfa the which they-call of Canal,
they-walked all the day, that rest not to-themselves they-give,
they-came that night in Calatayu[t]h to-camp.
sentences.i: They left Cella — the one they call 'of the Canal' — and marched all day without giving themselves rest, and that night they came to Calatayud and camped.
sentences.n: Ixieron, preterite of exir, 'went out'. la que dizen de Canal, 'the one they call [Cella] of the Canal': a local epithet; Pidal's footnote mentions Cella's Roman ruins but does not explain the name, and what Canal referred to is uncertain. andidieron, an old strong preterite of andar ('walked, marched'; modern anduvieron). todo 'l día = todo el día (the apostrophe marks the elision). vagar, 'leisure, rest' (noun): que vagar non se dan, 'for they allow themselves no rest'. Calatayu[t]h: the t is Pidal's.

sentences.i: Throughout all those lands the criers are sent out; troops gathered in vast numbers to these two kings, called Fáriz and Galve, and they go to besiege the good Çid in Alcocer.
sentences.n: los pregones dan: Pidal, 'despachan pregoneros', 'they dispatch heralds' (pregón, Latin praeconem, the crier who proclaims a muster). sobejanas de grandes: Pidal, literally 'excesivas de numerosas', 'numerous beyond measure'. Fáriz e Galve: the two Moorish commanders ('kings' in the sense of v. 637), fictional, says Pidal. al bueno de mio Çid, 'the good Çid' (literally 'the good one of my Çid', a stock idiom). van çercar, 'go to besiege'; le is the redundant object pronoun. grandes and Galve are á-e endings in the á tirada; the tirada closes on the plain á of çercar.

sentences.t:
Fincaron las tiendas e prendend las posadas,
creçen estos virtos, ca yentes son sobejanas.
sentences.l:
They-planted the tents and they-take the lodgings,
they-grow these hosts, for peoples are excessive.
sentences.i: They pitched their tents and took up quarters; these hosts keep growing, for there are vast numbers of them.
sentences.n: Tirada 33 (assonance á-a) — Fáriz and Galve besiege the Çid in Alcocer (Pidal: Fáriz y Galve cercan al Cid en Alcocer). Fincaron, 'planted, pitched' (fincar, f- for modern hincar). prendend = prenden, 'take': the odd final -d is in Pidal's text and is kept; prender posadas, 'to pitch camp', as v. 557 of the Çid. virtos, 'forces, armed hosts' (from Latin virtus in its late sense 'troops'); the precise sense is not certain, but 'hosts' fits creçen 'grow'. yentes = gentes, 'people, troops', with y- for g-. sobejanas, 'excessive, very numerous' (as v. 653).

sentences.i: The scouting parties the Moors send out go about clad in their armour day and night; many are the outposts, and great is the host.
sentences.n: arrobdas: Pidal, 'centinelas avanzados de un ejército', 'an army's advance sentinels', mounted pickets (an Arabic word). sacan, 'send out'. enbueltos … en armas, 'wrapped in arms', armed and ready at all hours. almofalla: Pidal, 'hueste, ejército', 'host, army' — the Arabic word also found as almohalla, almafalla, almahala, the same word as the 'mehalla' still used, he notes, for the armies of Morocco.

sentences.t: A los de mio Çid ya les tuellen el agua.
sentences.l: To those of my Çid already from-them they-take the water.
sentences.i: Now they cut off the water from my Çid's men.
sentences.n: tuellen, present of toller, 'take away': Pidal, toller el agua 'quitarla', 'to cut off the water' (cf. v. 555). les is the redundant dative; A los de mio Çid … les, 'from those of my Çid'.

sentences.t:
Mesnadas de mio Çid exir querién a batalla,
el que en buen ora nasco firme gelo vedava.
sentences.l:
Companies of my Çid to-go-out wanted to battle,
he who in good hour was-born firmly to-them-it forbade.
sentences.i: My Çid's companies wanted to sally out to battle, but he who was born in a good hour firmly forbade it.
sentences.n: Mesnadas, 'companies of retainers', a lord's armed household. exir … querién, 'wanted to go out' (querién, old imperfect, = querían). el que en buen ora nasco, the 'born in a good hour' form of the formula; nasco, old strong preterite of nacer, 'was born'. gelo = se lo (Old Spanish ge for le before lo/la), 'it to them': 'forbade it to them'. vedar, 'to forbid'.

sentences.t: Toviérongela en çerca complidas tres se[d]manas.
sentences.l: They-held-it-on-him in siege full three weeks.
sentences.i: They kept him under siege for three full weeks.
sentences.n: Toviérongela = tuviéronsela: tovieron (strong preterite of tener) + ge (= le, the Çid) + la. What la stands for is not explicit — probably the town or the siege itself ('they kept it in siege on him'); the sense is clear even if the referent is loose. complidas, 'full'. se[d]manas, the d supplied by Pidal (as v. 573).

sentences.t:
A cabo de tres se[d]manas, la quarta queríe entrar,
mio Çid con los sos tornós a acordar:
sentences.l:
At end of three weeks, the fourth wanted to-enter,
my Çid with the his-men turned-himself to consult:
sentences.i: At the end of three weeks, as the fourth was about to begin, my Çid turned to take counsel with his men:
sentences.n: Tirada 34 (assonance á) — the Çid takes counsel with his men; secret preparations; the Çid goes out to pitched battle against Fáriz and Galve; Per Vermudoz (Pero Vermúdez) strikes the first blows (Pidal: Consejo del Cid con los suyos. — Preparativos secretos. — El Cid sale a batalla campal contra Fáriz y Galve. — Pedro Vermúdez hiere los primeros golpes). Back to stressed á, with a few á-e lines (fablastes 677, raste 685, cabdales 698, mande 703 — see v. 625). querie entrar, 'was about to come in' (querer + infinitive of what is imminent, as v. 682, 696). tornós = tornóse, 'turned himself' (enclitic se cut to s). acordar, 'to come to an agreement, consult'.

sentences.t:
“el agua nos an vedada, exir nos ha el pan,
que nos queramos ir de noch no nos lo consintrán;
sentences.l:
“the water from-us they-have forbidden, will-go-out from-us the bread,
that we may-want to-go by night not to-us it they-will-allow;
sentences.i: “They have cut us off from the water, our bread will run out; and if we try to slip away by night they will not let us;
sentences.n: The Çid's speech runs to v. 670. vedada agrees with el agua (the participle agrees with its object, as a dexada, v. 582). exir nos ha el pan, split future: exir + nos + ha = 'the bread will go out on us', run short. Pidal quotes the Primera Crónica General's prose of the line: 'ell agua nos an ya tollido los moros et si assi estamos, puede nos fallescer el pan'. que nos queramos ir, 'if we wanted to go' (que + subjunctive as a condition, as v. 620). consintrán, syncopated future of consentir, 'they will allow'.

sentences.t:
grandes son los poderes por con ellos lidiar;
dezidme, cavalleros, cómmo vos plaze de far.”
sentences.l:
great are the forces for with them to-fight;
tell-me, knights, how to-you it-pleases to do.”
sentences.i: their forces are very great for us to fight against; tell me, knights, what you would have us do.”
sentences.n: poderes, 'armed forces'. por con ellos lidiar, 'for fighting with them' (por + infinitive, with the prepositional phrase placed first). dezidme, 'tell me'. cómmo vos plaze de far, 'how it pleases you to act'; far, a short form of fazer.

sentences.t:
Primero fabló Minaya, un cavallero de prestar:
“de Castiella la gentil exidos somos acá,
si con moros non lidiáremos, no nos darán del pan.
sentences.l:
First spoke Minaya, a knight of worth:
“from Castiella the noble gone-out we-are hither,
if with Moors not we-fight, not to-us they-will-give of-the bread.
sentences.i: Minaya spoke first, a knight of great worth: “We have come out here from noble Castile; if we do not fight the Moors, they will give us no bread.
sentences.n: Minaya is Álvar Fáñez, the Çid's right hand. de prestar, 'of worth, excellent' (literally 'to be of use'). Minaya's speech runs to v. 676; Pidal notes that Bello amplified the passage and called it 'uno de los bellos rasgos del Poema', 'one of the poem's fine touches'. Castiella la gentil, 'noble Castile' (gentil, 'of good lineage'). exidos somos, 'we are gone out' (exir takes ser, as a verb of motion). lidiáremos, future subjunctive, normal in Old Spanish si-clauses about the future. del pan, partitive, 'any bread'.

sentences.i: We are a good six hundred, and some few more; in the Creator's name, let it be no other way: let us go and strike them tomorrow.”
sentences.n: Bien somos nos seysçientos, 'we are fully six hundred'. ay = hay, 'there are'. no[m]bre: the m is Pidal's. que non passe por al: Pidal, non passar por al 'no pasar o hacerse de otro modo', 'not to happen otherwise' — 'there is no other remedy' (cf. vv. 710, 3367). al, 'other' (Latin aliud). vayámoslos ferir, 'let us go strike them' (vayamos + los; ferir = herir). cras, 'tomorrow' (Latin cras): aquel día de cras, 'tomorrow's day'.

sentences.t:
Dixo el Campeador: “a mi guisa fablastes;
ondrástesvos, Minaya, ca aver vos lo iedes de far.”
sentences.l:
Said the Campeador: “to my liking you-spoke;
you-honoured-yourself, Minaya, for to-have yourself it you-would of to-do.”
sentences.i: The Campeador said: “You have spoken as I would have it; you have done yourself honour, Minaya, as indeed you were bound to do.”
sentences.n: a mi guisa, 'after my own mind'. fablastes, 'you spoke' (preterite, 2nd person, vos form): an á-e ending in the á tirada. ondrástesvos = os honrasteis, 'you honoured yourself'. aver vos lo iedes de far, split conditional: aver + vos + lo + iedes (= habríais) + de far, 'you would have to do it'. Pidal explains far as standing in for ondrar: 'you have honoured yourself, Minaya, for you were sure to do so' ('pues sin duda habríais de honraros'), and argues that vos is the object, not the subject, since it sits between aver and the auxiliary iedes; the Primera Crónica read it simply as 'for you would have to do it', i.e. the plan was Minaya's to carry out. Pidal's reading is followed here.

sentences.t:
Todos los moros e las moras de fuera los manda echar,
que non sopiesse ninguno esta su poridad.
sentences.l:
All the Moors and the Moor-women from outside them he-orders to-cast,
that not should-know none this his secret.
sentences.i: He has all the Moors, men and women, put outside the walls, so that no one might learn this secret of his.
sentences.n: Pidal's rubric: preparativos secretos. The Moors are the townspeople he spared in v. 621. de fuera … echar, 'to put out'; manda, present, after the preterites (tense-mixing). sopiesse, imperfect subjunctive of saber. non … ninguno, double negative. poridad, 'secret' (from puridad, 'privacy, confidence'); esta su poridad, demonstrative + possessive.

sentences.i: Day and night they set about making ready. Next morning, as the sun was about to rise, my Çid is armed, with all the men he has;
sentences.n: piénssanse de adobar, 'they set about readying themselves' (pensar de + infinitive; adobar, 'to equip, prepare'). querie apuntar, 'was about to break' (apuntar, of the sun, 'to show its point'). armado es, 'is armed'. quantos que él ha, 'as many as he has' (aver, 'to have').

sentences.i: my Çid spoke, as you shall hear: “Let us all go out — let no one stay behind — except for two foot-soldiers only, to guard the gate;
sentences.n: odredes: Pidal, 'oiréis', 'you will hear' — the minstrel again addressing his audience; odir is the old form of oír. The Çid's speech runs to v. 691. iscamos, present subjunctive of exir; Pidal glosses the half-line 'todos salgamos fuera, que nadie quede', 'let us all go out, that no one remain'. nadi = nadie; non raste, 'not remain' (rastar, 'to stay behind'), an á-e ending in the á tirada. In Pidal's print the n of non in this line is damaged; it is read as non, which the grammar requires (double negative after nadi). pe[d]ones, 'foot-soldiers', the d supplied by Pidal.

sentences.t:
si nos muriéremos en campo, en castiello nos entrarán,
si vençiéremos la batalla, creçremos en rictad.
sentences.l:
if we should-die in field, in castle on-us they-will-enter,
if we-should-win the battle, we-shall-grow in riches.
sentences.i: if we die in the field, they will come into the castle on us; if we win the battle, we shall grow in wealth.
sentences.n: muriéremos, vençiéremos, future subjunctives in the si-clauses (as lidiáremos, v. 673). en campo, 'in the open field', the batalla campal of Pidal's rubric. entrarán, 'they will enter'. creçremos, syncopated future of creçer. rictad: Pidal, 'riqueza', 'riches'.

sentences.i: And you, Per Vermudoz, take my banner; as you are a true man, you will bear it loyally; but do not spur forward with it unless I give you the order.”
sentences.n: Per Vermu[doz]: the -doz is Pidal's (as v. 611): Pero (Pedro) Bermúdez, the Çid's standard-bearer. la mi seña, article + possessive. sodes = sois. tener la edes, split future: tener + la + edes (= la tendréis), 'you will hold it'. ar[t]h: Pidal, 'mal arte, engaño', 'evil craft, deceit'; sin art, 'faithfully' — the t is his. aguijedes, 'you spur' (negative command in the subjunctive). mandar: the future subjunctive mandare cut to mandar, 'if I do not command it'. The order, given here, is what Per Vermudoz will break in v. 704.

sentences.t: Al Çid besó la mano, la seña va tomar.
sentences.l: To-the Çid he-kissed the hand, the banner goes to-take.
sentences.i: He kissed the Çid's hand and took the banner.
sentences.n: Pidal: being given the standard to carry in battle was a distinction, acknowledged by kissing the hand, as one did on receiving a favour (una merced). va tomar, 'goes to take' = 'takes' (ir + infinitive without a, a narrative periphrasis).

sentences.t:
Abrieron las puertas, fuera un salto dan;
viéronlo las arrobdas de los moros, al almofalla se van tornar.
sentences.l:
They-opened the gates, outside a leap they-give;
they-saw-it the outposts of the Moors, to-the host they-go to-turn.
sentences.i: They opened the gates and burst out; the Moorish pickets saw it and turned back to the main host.
sentences.n: un salto dan, 'they make a sally' (dar salto, as v. 584). viéronlo, 'they saw it' (vieron + lo). arrobdas … almofalla: the pickets and the main army (vv. 658, 660); Pidal: the outposts fall back on the host. se van tornar, 'they turn back' (ir + infinitive again).

sentences.i: What a scramble there is among the Moors! They rushed to arm again; at the din of the drums the earth seemed about to split; you could have seen Moors arming, hurrying into their battle lines.
sentences.n: ¡Qué priessa va en los moros!, 'what haste goes among the Moors'. tornáronse a armar, 'they armed themselves again'. ante: Pidal says it expresses the cause, like Latin prae, 'because of' (compare modern 'ante la imposibilidad de huir, se rindieron'). roído = ruido; atamores = tambores, 'drums' (Arabic). querié quebrar, 'was about to break' (as v. 665). veriedes, conditional of ver, 'you would have seen' — the minstrel's call to his audience to picture the scene. az, 'battle line, rank' (Latin acies); entrar en az, 'to form up'.

sentences.t:
De parte de los moros dos señas ha cabdales,
e [los] pe[n]dones mezclados, ¿qui los podrié contar?
sentences.l:
On part of the Moors two banners there-are principal,
and [the] pe[n]nons mingled, who them could count?
sentences.i: On the Moors' side there are two chief standards, and pennons of every sort besides — who could count them?
sentences.n: ha, impersonal 'there is/are' (aver). cabdales, 'chief, principal' (Latin capitalis): an á-e ending in the á tirada. Pidal: the two chief standards are those of the two army corps of Fáriz and Galve; the pendones mezclados, 'mixed' or various pennons, are, as the Primera Crónica puts it, 'los otros pendones daquellos pueblos ayuntados allí', those of the frontier towns (vv. 640, 653). [los] and the n of pe[n]dones are Pidal's. qui = quién; podrié = podría.

sentences.t:
La[s] azes de los moros yas mueven adelant,
por a mio Çid e a los sos a manos los tomar.
sentences.l:
The[s] lines of the Moors already-themselves move forward,
for to my Çid and to the his-men by hands them to-take.
sentences.i: The Moorish battle lines are already moving forward, to take my Çid and his men with their bare hands.
sentences.n: La[s]: the s is Pidal's. azes, plural of az, 'battle lines'. yas = ya se, 'already themselves' (mueven se, 'move'). adelant = adelante, cut. por … tomar, 'in order to take'; a manos tomar, 'to take by hand', i.e. capture outright, without a real fight. a mio Çid e a los sos … los: personal a, with the redundant los.

sentences.t:
“Quedas se[e]d, me[s]nadas, aquí en este logar,
non derranche ninguno fata que yo lo mande.”
sentences.l:
“Still be, companies, here in this place,
not break-ranks none until that I it command.”
sentences.i: “Stand firm, my companies, here in this place; let no one break ranks until I give the order.”
sentences.n: The speaker is not named; it is the Çid (cf. v. 691). Quedas se[e]d, 'be still, hold your ground' (quedo, 'still'; seed, imperative of ser — the second e and the s of me[s]nadas are Pidal's). derranche, subjunctive of derranchar, 'to break ranks, leave the line'. fata = hasta, 'until'. mande ends in á-e in the á tirada.

sentences.t:
Aquel Per Vermu[doz] non lo pudo endurar,
la seña tiene en mano, conpeçó de espolonar:
sentences.l:
That Per Vermu[doz] not it could endure,
the banner he-holds in hand, began to spur:
sentences.i: But Per Vermudoz could not bear it; the banner in his hand, he began to spur forward:
sentences.n: Aquel, 'that' (a demonstrative of emphasis, 'that Per Vermudoz'). endurar: Pidal, 'sufrir, resistir', 'to endure, hold back'. conpeçó de espolonar, 'began to spur' (conpeçar = comenzar; espolonar, from espolón 'spur').

sentences.i: “The Creator be with you, loyal Çid Campeador! I am going to plant your banner in that biggest battle line; and you who owe it your service, I shall see how you come to its rescue.”
sentences.n: Per Vermudoz's words. vos vala, 'may He help you' (valer, 'to protect, aid', present subjunctive). Pidal prints 'leal!' with no opening ¡ here (contrast ¡non sea, v. 709); the text is kept as he prints it. Vo = voy, 'I go'; vo meter, 'I go to put'. mayor az, 'greatest line', the thickest of the enemy's ranks. los que el debdo avedes, 'you who have the duty' (debdo = deuda, 'debt, obligation' — the vassal's bond to the lord's banner). acorr[a]des, subjunctive of acorrer, 'succour, come to the aid of' (the a is Pidal's); la is the banner. The challenge forces the whole company to follow.

sentences.t:
Dixo el Campeador: “¡non sea, por caridad!”
Respuso Per Vermu[doz]: “non rastará por al.”
sentences.l:
Said the Campeador: “not let-it-be, for charity!”
Answered Per Vermu[doz]: “not it-will-remain for other.”
sentences.i: The Campeador said: “No, for charity's sake!” Per Vermudoz answered: “It cannot be otherwise.”
sentences.n: non sea, 'let it not be'. por caridad, 'for charity's sake', i.e. 'for God's sake, I beg you'. Respuso, strong preterite of responder. non rastará por al: Pidal, 'no quedará de otro modo', 'it will not be otherwise', 'it cannot fail to be' (rastar, 'to remain', as v. 685; al, 'other'; cf. v. 675).

sentences.t: Espolonó el cavallo, e metiól en el mayor az.
sentences.l: He-spurred the horse, and put-him in the greatest line.
sentences.i: He set spurs to his horse and drove it into the thickest of their ranks.
sentences.n: metiól = metiólo (metió + le, the horse; the pronoun cut to l). en el mayor az: the 'greatest line' of v. 707.

sentences.t:
Moros le reçiben por la seña ganar,
danle grandes colpes, mas nol pueden falssar.
sentences.l:
Moors him receive for the banner to-win,
they-give-him great blows, but not-him they-can pierce.
sentences.i: The Moors close round him to win the banner and deal him great blows, but they cannot break through his armour.
sentences.n: reçiben, 'receive, meet' (the charge). por … ganar, 'in order to win'. danle = le dan. colpes = golpes. nol = no le, 'not him'. falssar: Pidal — in full falssar las armas (v. 2391), falssar la loriga (v. 728) or la guarnizón (v. 3681) — 'to break or shatter the defensive armour': they cannot pierce his mail.

sentences.t: Dixo el Campeador: “¡valelde, por caridad!”
sentences.l: Said the Campeador: “help-him, for charity!”
sentences.i: The Campeador said: “Help him, for charity's sake!”
sentences.n: valelde = valedle, 'help him' (imperative valed + le, with the d and l swapped — a common metathesis). The Çid's ¡non sea! of v. 709 becomes a cry to save his standard-bearer; the next tirada (35) opens on the charge to rescue him.
